title: Consent-aware Redaction and Retention Orchestrator for Console Analytics
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a resilient service and orchestration layer that enforces consent-driven retention TTLs and performs deterministic PII redaction across Console usage analytics. The system must support configurable retention policies per customer/org, provide auditable deletions and redactions, and integrate with existing pipeline components (Kafka ingestion, raw event store, analytics warehouse).
background: Current analytics pipelines persist event payloads that may contain user-identifiable tokens or metadata. Existing ad-hoc scrubbing jobs are inconsistent across shards and lack a unified audit trail. Regulatory and enterprise customers require: per-org retention based on consent or contract, proof-of-deletion, and ability to redact specific attributes retrospectively.
goals: Implement a consent-aware orchestrator that issues redaction or deletion commands tied to org retention policies
Ensure redaction is deterministic and reversible only in audit metadata (no plaintext recovery)
Provide an immutable audit log of actions with verifiable timestamps and operator/automated actor IDs
Expose APIs for on-demand erasure requests and status tracking (idempotent and rate-limited)
Integrate into streaming pipeline so new events are evaluated for redaction at ingest and at scheduled retention sweeps
non_goals: Do not attempt to replace the canonical event schema for all products
This ticket does not include front-end Console UI for self-serve data-retention changes (separate PM ticket)
proposed_solution: Introduce a Retention Orchestrator microservice that: (1) maintains per-org retention policy metadata (consent state, TTLs, attribute-level redaction rules), (2) publishes idempotent delete/redact commands to a dedicated Kafka topic 'analytics.retention.commands', (3) coordinates workers that perform redaction at three layers — ingest-time scrubber, row-level redactor for the raw event store, and warehouse-level obfuscator for derived tables. Redaction will use a two-layer approach: rules-based regex patterns for well-known tokens and a lightweight ML model for fuzzy PII detection. All operations write entries to an append-only audit stream with event hashes and operator identity. The orchestrator will support dry-run mode and retention-audit exports for compliance teams.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Schema for retention policy store (Postgres) + API definitions
Week 2: Orchestrator service scaffolding + publish/subscribe contract to Kafka topic
Week 3: Implement ingest-time scrubber hook in ingestion service (best-effort redaction) and unit tests
Week 4: Worker that applies row-level redaction to raw event store (S3/Parquet shards) with sharded concurrency
Week 5: Warehouse obfuscation orchestrator for BigQuery/Redshift derived tables
Week 6: Audit log export, retries, and end-to-end QA + runbooks
Rolling: Security review and compliance signoff before release
data_flow: Ingest -> ingest-scrubber -> raw-event-store (S3) -> retention-orchestrator reads policy -> issues command to analytics.retention.commands -> redaction-workers read command and mutate data store or emit masked copies -> writes audit record to analytics.retention.audit (append-only) -> orchestrator updates job status
storage_considerations: Retention metadata: Postgres with encryption at rest. Audit stream: write-through to an immutable append-only S3 prefix + compacted index in DynamoDB for quick lookup. Redaction markers: rows are replaced with deterministic HMACs for removed fields to allow linking without storing plaintext.
observability: Expose Prometheus metrics: retention_jobs_total, redaction_rate, redaction_error_rate, deletion_latency_seconds.histogram, retention_backlog_gauge. Create Grafana dashboards: 'Retention Orchestrator Overview', 'Backlog by Org', 'Failed Redactions by Reason'. Send critical alerts to PagerDuty for stuck jobs > 24h and >1% error rate on redaction workers.
security_and_compliance: All API operations require mTLS and OAuth tokens with scope 'retention:manage'. Access to audit exports gated by RBAC and customer contract checks. Key material for HMACs stored in KMS. Security to perform threat modeling and PAM review prior to rollout.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scrubber rules, integration test that runs end-to-end on a staging Kafka+S3 pipeline, property-based tests for idempotency of erase commands, and load test to validate worker throughput at expected production scale. Run a privacy canary: seed synthetic PII and verify redaction coverage >= 99% for known patterns.
migration_strategy: Run in dry-run mode for 2 weeks to build audit evidence comparing existing ad-hoc jobs vs orchestrator output. Then enable gradual on-boarding by org (pilot cohort of 5 orgs) before global flip. Maintain compatibility with legacy deletion topics for 90 days.
rollback_plan: If systemic issues appear, pause orchestrator, revert to legacy scrubbing jobs, and replay commands from audit stream after fixes. Ensure all deletions are idempotent to avoid double-hard-delete.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can create/update/delete per-org policy via API
Retention commands are published and consumed with at-least-once delivery semantics
Audit stream contains immutable entries for 100% of actions with operator or automation identity
Pilot orgs see no more than 0.5% increase in ingestion latency with ingest-time scrubber enabled
End-to-end erase job completes within SLA (24 hours) for orgs with < 10M events
Automated privacy canary validates redaction coverage >= 99% for seeded patterns
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-redaction causing analytics regressions. Mitigation: dry-run mode and attribute-level allowlists; enable a safelist toggle per org
Risk: Long-running jobs create backlog. Mitigation: autoscale worker fleet and implement per-org rate limits and backpressure signals
Risk: Incomplete audit evidence. Mitigation: append-only audit stream with checksums and nightly consistency job
notes_and_updates: 2025-01-09: Initial design review with infra and security. Security requested threat model and KMS plan (assigned to Ravi).
2025-01-13: Prototype ingest-scrubber implemented and benchmarked; 0.3ms median added latency observed.
2025-01-17: Decided on HMAC deterministic masking instead of reversible encryption for removed fields to reduce attack surface.
2025-01-20: Pilot cohort list finalized (orgs: redwood-sdk, partner-analytics, example-enterprise). Scheduling pilot onboarding in Cycle 2025-W04.
